prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Kansas City Missouri for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on your facts (severity of injuries, insurance limits, whether fault is disputed, whether you want trial vs settlement, etc.). I can, however, help you find a top attorney and tell you how to choose one.

Quick guidance
- Start local: pick a Kansas City attorney who regularly handles car-accident personal injury cases and tries cases in local courts.
- Look for results: large settlements/verdicts and a track record handling cases like yours (similar injuries, serious vs minor, uninsured/underinsured motorist claims).
- Trial experience matters: many cases settle, but you want a lawyer who will and can take your case to trial if necessary.
- Communication and resources: firm should promptly return calls, advance litigation costs, and have medical/forensic experts available.
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Confirm percent, who pays litigation costs if you lose, and get it in writing.

Where to search and vet lawyers
- Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, Avvo/Justia profiles (peer reviews, client ratings).
- Best Lawyers lists and local “Top Lawyers” directories.
- Missouri Bar Lawyer Referral Service and the Jackson County Bar Association.
- Google and Yelp reviews, plus any published verdicts/settlements in local news.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled in KC in the last year? How many went to trial?
- What results have you obtained for cases like mine?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or staff)?
- What is your fee and how are costs handled?
- What is a realistic range for my case and how long will it take?
- Can you provide references from past clients?

Important practical points
- Missouri’s statute of limitations for most personal-injury claims is 5 years (act promptly—deadlines and special rules apply).
- Bring police report, photos, medical bills/records, insurance info, and any wage statements to consultations.
- Get at least 2–3 consultations and compare.

If you want, tell me:
- the city/zip in Kansas City,
- a brief description of the accident and injuries,
and I’ll prepare a short list of well‑rated Kansas City personal-injury attorneys/firms you can contact and a script/email template to use for consultations. Which would you prefer?
